title: Examining the Views of Educators in General Secondary Education Institutions on the Incorporation of Artificial Intelligence into the Learning Process
venue: Immersive Technologies in Education: Collection of Materials of the III International Scientific and Practical Conference
extended_summary:
This conference paper examines how educators in general secondary education institutions view the integration of artificial intelligence into teaching and learning. The study is motivated by the broader digital transformation of education and asks how ready the pedagogical community is to adopt AI, what benefits teachers perceive, and what risks or barriers they associate with its use.

The author used a survey distributed through professional communities in Google Forms. The survey asked teachers about their attitudes toward AI integration, prior experience using AI tools, perceived benefits, and perceived limitations or risks. Reported benefits included automation of routine tasks, individualized learning, easier access to information, and support for teachers' professional work. Reported concerns included overreliance on technology, reduced independent thinking, inequality in access, privacy concerns, and the potential weakening of live teacher-student interaction.

The population consisted of 31 pedagogical staff members from general secondary education institutions in the Fastiv city territorial community. Participants included teachers from several subject areas as well as educational support personnel. This is a school-sector study about educator perceptions; it does not test ChatGPT or any AI intervention on students, and it does not focus on writing instruction or student writing outcomes.

The paper concludes that most respondents were broadly positive about AI's potential in education, though many also expressed uncertainty and a need for more training and discussion. The author recommends additional support, awareness-building, and professional development for teachers. For evidence-synthesis purposes, this paper is not a high-school writing-feedback effectiveness study and should not be included as evidence on ChatGPT-based writing feedback outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conference proceedings conceptual paper describing possibilities of immersive technologies and AI for assessment. It does not report a controlled empirical study, no analyzable sample for the AI claims, and no outcome statistics or effect sizes.
impact_tier_rationale: Impact is unclear because the paper makes forward-looking claims without reporting empirical effects. There is no credible quantitative estimate of impact on learners or institutions.

interventions.use_case: Use of ChatGPT/AI as a simulated applicant/interview partner and as an automated scorer for open-ended assessment tasks in professional qualification assessment; discussed conceptually as part of immersive/AI-enabled assessment rather than empirically evaluated.

Use of immersive simulators and virtual reality environments to assess vocational skills and learning outcomes for professional qualification seekers (e.g., pilot simulators, electrician VR helmet, maritime simulators, driving simulation).
